title: Near future and simple future
spec: Verbs: tenses: immediate/near future; simple future
summary: Near future: present of aller + infinitive means 'going to': Je vais réviser ce soir. Ils vont partir demain.

In the negative, ne ... pas goes round the part of aller: Nous n'allons pas sortir ce week-end. A reflexive pronoun stays in front of the infinitive and matches the subject: Je vais me coucher. Nous allons nous lever tôt.
Simple future of regular verbs: infinitive + -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont: je jouerai, tu finiras, nous regarderons.
-re verbs drop the final e before the endings: prendre → je prendrai, attendre → ils attendront.
Irregular stems take the same endings: être → ser-, avoir → aur-, aller → ir-, faire → fer-: je serai, nous aurons, ils iront, il fera beau.
More irregular stems: pouvoir → pourr-, vouloir → voudr-, devoir → devr-, savoir → saur-, venir → viendr-, voir → verr-, envoyer → enverr-, il faut → il faudra.
Every future stem ends in r. Verbs like acheter add a grave accent: j'achèterai, elle achètera.
After quand (and lorsque, dès que), use the future when the action is still to come, even though English uses the present: Quand j'aurai dix-huit ans, j'apprendrai à conduire.
Use the near future for plans and things about to happen, and the simple future for predictions and things further ahead; using both in your writing shows range.
Don't confuse the future (je serai = I will be) with the conditional (je serais = I would be).

cards.front: How do you form the near future (le futur proche)?
cards.back: Present tense of aller + infinitive: je vais jouer, tu vas jouer, il/elle/on va jouer, nous allons jouer, vous allez jouer, ils/elles vont jouer. It means 'going to': Je vais jouer au tennis = I'm going to play tennis.

cards.prompt: Demain, nous ___ au parc avec le chien.
cards.en: Tomorrow we are going to play in the park with the dog.
cards.why: Near future = present of aller (nous allons) + the infinitive, which does not change: allons jouer.

cards.prompt: Je suis très fatigué, alors je ___ tout de suite.
cards.en: I'm very tired, so I'm going to go to bed straight away.
cards.why: In the near future the reflexive pronoun stays in front of the infinitive and matches the subject: je vais me coucher (not je vais se coucher).

cards.instruction: Rewrite the sentence in the near future (aller + infinitive).
cards.en: I am going to do my homework.
cards.why: Put the present of aller (je vais) in front and change fais to the infinitive faire.

cards.instruction: Rewrite the sentence in the near future, keeping it negative.
cards.prompt: Ils ne prennent pas le train.
answers: Ils ne vont pas prendre le train.
cards.en: They are not going to take the train.
cards.why: ne ... pas goes round the conjugated part (vont); the infinitive prendre comes after pas.

cards.front: How do you form the simple future of regular verbs?
cards.back: Take the infinitive and add -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont. -re verbs drop their final e first. jouer → je jouerai, finir → tu finiras, vendre → il vendra, regarder → nous regarderons, choisir → vous choisirez, attendre → elles attendront. It means 'will': je jouerai = I will play.

cards.prompt: L'année prochaine, ma sœur ___ ses études à Lyon.
cards.en: Next year my sister will start her studies in Lyon.
cards.why: Regular -er verb: infinitive commencer + -a for elle. No cedilla is needed because the c is followed by e.

cards.prompt: Demain matin, tu ___ le bus de huit heures.
cards.en: Tomorrow morning you will take the eight o'clock bus.
cards.why: -re verbs drop the final e of the infinitive before the ending: prendr- + -as.

cards.prompt: Mes grands-parents nous ___ à l'aéroport samedi prochain.
cards.en: My grandparents will wait for us at the airport next Saturday.
cards.why: attendre drops its final e: attendr- + -ont for a plural subject (ils).

cards.front: Which common verbs have an irregular stem in the simple future?
cards.back: être → ser- (je serai), avoir → aur- (j'aurai), aller → ir- (j'irai), faire → fer- (je ferai), pouvoir → pourr- (je pourrai), vouloir → voudr- (je voudrai), devoir → devr- (je devrai), savoir → saur- (je saurai), venir → viendr- (je viendrai), voir → verr- (je verrai), envoyer → enverr- (j'enverrai), falloir → il faudra. The endings are the same as for regular verbs.

cards.prompt: L'été prochain, nous ___ en Italie pour les vacances.
cards.en: Next summer we will go to Italy for the holidays.
cards.why: aller has the irregular future stem ir-: nous irons.

cards.prompt: Selon la météo, demain il ___ beau dans le sud de la France.
cards.en: According to the weather forecast, it will be fine in the south of France tomorrow.
cards.why: faire has the irregular future stem fer-: il fera beau = it will be fine.

cards.prompt: Le mois prochain, mes parents ___ une voiture électrique.
cards.en: Next month my parents will have an electric car.
cards.why: avoir has the irregular future stem aur-: ils auront.

cards.prompt: Quand j'aurai dix-huit ans, je ___ passer mon permis de conduire.
cards.en: When I am eighteen, I will be able to take my driving test.
cards.why: pouvoir has the irregular future stem pourr- (double r): je pourrai.

cards.prompt: Ce soir, tu ___ ranger ta chambre avant de sortir.
cards.en: This evening you will have to tidy your room before going out.
cards.why: devoir has the irregular future stem devr-: tu devras = you will have to.

cards.instruction: Rewrite the sentence in the simple future.
cards.en: My cousins will know how to swim.
cards.why: savoir has the irregular future stem saur-: ils sauront.

cards.front: Translate: 'When I am older, I will live abroad.' What is the trap?
cards.back: Quand je serai plus âgé(e), j'habiterai à l'étranger. After quand, French uses the future when the action is still to come; English uses the present ('when I am'). Writing 'quand je suis plus âgé' for a future idea is a classic mistake.

cards.prompt: Quand je ___ grand, je deviendrai pilote.
cards.en: When I grow up, I will become a pilot.
cards.why: quand + future: the action is still to come, so French uses the future (je serai) where English uses the present.

cards.prompt: Quand Paul ___ à la maison ce soir, il t'enverra un message.
cards.en: When Paul gets home this evening, he will send you a message.
cards.why: The main verb (enverra) is in the future, so the verb after quand must be future too: rentrera, not rentre. (The future perfect sera rentré is also correct.)

cards.prompt: Quand vous viendrez à Paris, vous ___ la tour Eiffel.
cards.en: When you come to Paris, you will see the Eiffel Tower.
cards.why: voir has the irregular future stem verr-: vous verrez. Notice viendrez (venir → viendr-) after quand as well.

cards.prompt: Ma cousine nous ___ des photos de son voyage au Canada.
cards.en: My cousin will send us photos of her trip to Canada.
cards.why: envoyer has the irregular future stem enverr-: elle enverra.

cards.instruction: Change the near future to the simple future.
cards.en: We will have to leave early.
cards.why: falloir is only used with il; its future is il faudra (stem faudr-).

cards.prompt: Demain, ma mère ___ du pain à la boulangerie.
cards.en: Tomorrow my mother will buy some bread at the baker's.
cards.why: acheter changes e to è in its future stem (achèter-), so elle achètera.

cards.front: je serai or je serais? How do you tell the simple future from the conditional?
cards.back: Both use the same stem. The future has the endings -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont: je serai = I will be. The conditional has the imperfect endings -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient: je serais = I would be. The je forms can sound alike, so check the spelling carefully when you write.
